Table

Source: R/table.R
bb_table.Rd

A table whose rows are as tall as their content at the width the table gets. Every cell can hold text (with per-column style and alignment, and per-cell overrides through [cell()]) or any block: [bb_status()], [bb_dot()], images, plots with a height, even nested stacks.

Usage

bb_table(
  rows,
  header = NULL,
  widths = NULL,
  align = "left",
  col_style = NULL,
  header_style = NULL,
  style = table_style(),
  min_row_heights = 0,
  header_case = c("none", "upper")
)

Arguments

rows

A list of rows (each a list with one entry per column), or a `data.frame`.

header

Optional header labels; `NULL` for no header row. For a data frame, defaults to its column names.

widths

Column widths as in [bb_cols()]: `NULL` (equal), numeric proportions, or a unit vector mixing absolute and `"null"` widths.

align

Per-column alignment (`"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`), recycled.

col_style

Per-column text style(s): one [text_style()] / role name, or a list recycled over columns. Layered over `style$body_style`.

header_style

Header text style; overrides `style$header_style`.

style

A [table_style()].

min_row_heights

Minimum body row height(s), recycled.

header_case

Letter case for header labels (`"none"`, `"upper"`).

Value

A block. Inside [bb_cols()] with `sync_rows = TRUE`, side-by-side tables share row heights.

Examples

bb_table(list(list("DTPCV3", "94.1%"), list("MCV1", cell("No data", text_style(color = "faint")))),
         header = c("Vaccine", "Coverage"), widths = c(3, 1), align = c("left", "right"))
#> <bb_table>
